MEMORANDUM ON ADOLFO CARPI.

Mr. Adolfo Carpi, Italian Impressario, has organised
many operatic and revue companies with which he has toured
the Far East on various occasions since 1923.

During 1929/30 he shared an apartment at 1 Canton
Road with M.A. Lourie Ettingoff, an enthusiastic Soviet
worker, but enquiries failed to establish the existence
between them of any relations of a political character.
Previously, the French Police, acting on the instructions
of the Italian Consul, effected a search of Carpi's residence
but were unable to unearth any evidence on which to substan-
tiate the suspicion that he was operating as a Soviet agent.

In June 1932, it was learned that Carpi and Francesco
Contini, another Italian, were living up to a standard of
people drawing $1,000.00 per month and making frequent trips
to other parts of the Far East, though neither of them had
done any legitimate work for about 3 years. It was further
learned that Contini, who arrived in Shanghai during 1928 as
a chorus singer in an opera company under the management of
Carpi, had visited Italy during 1932 and there came under
suspicion of being connected with the III International.

The movements of these two persons were closely checked
during June 1932, and it became strongly suspected that their
efforts in the operatic and revue world served as cloaks for
purposes identified with the smuggling of arms and drugs.
This suspicion remains unconfirmed.

Carpi last staged an opera locally during October 1932,
when the gross takings barely covered the expenses incurred.

关于阿道夫·卡尔皮（ADOLFO CARPI）的备忘录。

阿道夫·卡尔皮先生，意大利剧院经理，自1923年以来曾多次组织歌剧和歌舞团在远东各地巡回演出。

在1929/30年间，他与 M.A. Lourie Ettingoff 共同居住在广东路1号的一套公寓内，后者是一名热情的苏联工作人员，但调查未能确立他们之间存在任何政治性质的关系。此前，法国警方根据意大利领事的指示，对卡尔皮的住所进行了搜查，但未能找到任何证据来证实他是苏联特工的怀疑。

1932年6月，获悉卡尔皮和另一名意大利人弗朗切斯科·孔蒂尼（Francesco Contini）的生活水平相当于月收入1,000.00美元的人群，并频繁前往远东其他地区，尽管两人在大约3年内均未从事任何正当工作。进一步获悉，孔蒂尼于1928年作为卡尔皮管理的歌剧团合唱歌手抵达上海，曾于1932年访问意大利，并在那里被怀疑与第三国际有关联。

1932年6月期间，这两人的行踪受到严密监控，人们强烈怀疑他们在歌剧和歌舞界的活动只是为与武器和毒品走私有关的目的作掩护。这一怀疑仍未得到证实。

卡尔皮上一次在当地上演歌剧是在1932年10月，当时的总收入勉强覆盖支出。当时他仍居住在广东路1号，与 U. Azzaretti（文图里公司经理，该公司为食品及酒类商人，地址为四川路116号）、库尔特·诺尔（Kurt Noll）医生及其（卡尔皮的）妻子合住一套公寓。该公寓于1933年8月由众人搬空，当时卡尔皮离开上海，据推测是前往新加坡。他的妻子留在上海并

page_data.en:
( 2 )

obtained employment at Dr. K. Noll's Hospital on Avenue
Joffre, and it is confirmed that she has definitely severed
her connections with Carpi.

Carpi and his operatic troupe returned to Shanghai
from Singapore on February 3, 1934 after having been refused
a visa for admission into Netherlands India.

Contini was last heard of in August 1933, when he
vacated his apartment at 690 Avenue Road (which he rented
and used in addition to sharing a flat at 1 Canton Road)
for an unknown destination.
page_data.zh:
( 2 )

在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）的 K. Noll 医生医院找到了工作，且已证实她确实断绝了与卡尔皮的关系。

卡尔皮及其歌剧团在被拒绝签发进入荷属东印度的签证后，于1934年2月3日从新加坡返回上海。

最后一次听到孔蒂尼的消息是在1933年8月，当时他退租了爱文义路（Avenue Road）690号的公寓（除了合租广东路1号的公寓外，他还租用并使用该公寓），前往一个未知的目的地。

With reference to the remarks of the Officer i/c
Special Branch on the attached file, I have to state that
a party of forty-seven members of Carpi's Light Opera Co.
travelling as second class passengers, arrived in Shanghai
from Tongku on October 14, 1932 by the s.s. "Shengking."

In view of the fact that there is strong reason to
believe that Adolfo Carpi's various operatic and revue
enterprises merely serve as cloaks for illicit purposes identi-
fied with the smuggling of drugs, enquiries were made which
go to show that the former ventures are definitely not
financially successful, indicating that Carpi must derive
an income from other sources, in order to live as he does.

In connection with the season that opened at the Em-
bassy Theatre on Tuesday October 18, 1932, it is interesting
to note that the artistes and orchestra comprising the com-
pany were recruited by Carpi in Harbin. It is said that
several members are Soviet citizens, but up to the present
no confirmation of this statement has been obtained..

The company gave recitals in Harbin and Tientsin
before coming to Shanghai. The cost of the passage from Tien-
tsin to Shanghai amounted to $1410.00, which was paid by
Carpi.

The gross takings for the first four opening nights
at the Embassy were $1181, $932, $514 and $582 respectively -
$3209 in all. Against this must be written $1600 - the cost
for hiring the Embassy being $400 per night - leaving a
profit of $1609.

salaries, wardrobe (which is an extensive one), advertising

With reference to the endorsement of the Officer i/c
Special Branch on the attached report, I have to state that
diligent and exhaustive enquiries over a lengthy period
have failed to ascertain the means whereby CARPI and CON-
TINI derive their livelihood.

In view of the discreet nature of the enquiry, and
bearing in mind the 'alarmist' attitude that has been met
with in dealings with members of the local members of the
Italian community, it was deemed advisable to discontinue
investigations in order that no inkling of the enquiry
might reach the ears of the people under discussion.

It would appear that Contini, who is financed by
Carpi, is a small fry in the latter's affairs. It is said
that both Carpi and Contini gamble very heavily in Shang-
hai, but the location of the haunts that they frequent cannot
be ascertained. It is also reported that Carpi's various
efforts in the operatic and revue worlds merely serve as
cloaks for purposes identified with the smuggling of arms
and drugs, but unfortunately, this information cannot be
confirmed.

This matter will be born in mind and further enquiries
will be made, and in the event of any reliable information
coming to light, another report will be immediately sub-

鉴于调查性质的谨慎性，并考虑到在与当地意大利
社区成员打交道时遇到的“大惊小怪”态度，认为宜
停止调查，以免被讨论对象察觉调查风声。

看来由卡尔皮资助的孔蒂尼在卡尔皮的事务中
只是个小角色。据说卡尔皮和孔蒂尼在上海
赌博数额巨大，但无法查明他们经常出没的场所。
另有报告称，卡尔皮在歌剧和歌舞剧界的各种努力
仅作为与武器和毒品走私有关的目的的掩护，但不幸的是，
此信息无法得到证实。

此事将铭记在心，并将进行进一步调查，若有可靠信息
出现，将立即提交另一份报告。

J. A. Giles

Watch maintained at 1 Canton Road in connection with
CARPI and CONTINI

June 19, 1932.        Nobody of any importance was seen to
                      enter or leave the premises.

June 20, 1932.        At 10.50 a.m. CARPI and CONTINI were seen
                      to leave the premises and make their way to the
                      Robert Dollar Line Building, Canton Road, which
                      CARPI entered whilst CONTINI remained outside.
                      Ten minutes later they proceeded to the Central
                      Arcade, entering by the Nanking-Szechuen Roads
                      entrance; they both made their way upstairs and
                      remained there for about five minutes.
                      CONTINI then returned to 1 Canton Road
                      whilst CARPI made his way by tramcar to the
                      Embassy Theatre. He had not left the theatre
                      by 1.30 p.m. when the agent took his tiffin.
                      At 2.35 p.m. CONTINI left 1 Canton Road
                      and proceeded to 39 Canton Road - a block of
                      offices - where he remained until 3 p.m.
                      He was then seen to make his way back to 1
                      Canton Road. At 3.10 p.m. he walked to
                      452 Kiangse Road - offices - which he entered,
                      remaining there for but a few minutes.
                      Leaving these premises, he proceeded to F.
                      Venturi & Co., 116 Szechuen Road and later
                      left for 35 Jinkee Road - premises housing a
                      block of offices. Some 10 minutes later he
                      proceeded to his residence at 1 Canton Road.
                      Neither was then seen up till 6.30 p.m.
                      when the watch was terminated.

June 21, 1932.        At 9.45 a.m. CARPI and CONTINI were seen
                      to leave 1 Canton Road when they made their way
                      to the Auction Rooms of Noel, Murray & Co.,
                      11 Hankow Road where they remained for some 10
                      minutes. Leaving, they made their way to the
                      American Express Co., 15 Kiukiang Road. CARPI
                      entered the premises whilst CONTINI remained
                      outside. Some minutes later CARPI came out
                      and with CONTINI proceeded to Kiukiang and
                      Kiangse Roads corner where the former was seen
                      to hand the latter some money.
                      Parting company at about 10.10 a.m. CONTINI
                      made his way by bus to the Kavkaz Hotel, 939
                      Bubbling Well Road. At 11 a.m. he returned to
                      the Central District and made his way to the
                      Auction Rooms of L. Moore and Co., Kiangse
                      Road where he met CARPI again.
                      They then boarded a western bound bus
                      which moved too quickly for the agent to follow.
                      At 3 p.m. CARPI returned to 1 Canton Road
                      and remained on the premises until 9.20 p.m.
                      when, accompanied by his wife, he made his way
                      along the Bund to the Bund Gardens; retracing
                      their steps, a halt was called at the Cinderella
                      Restaurant, Szechuen Road which they entered
                      and remained in until 11.50 p.m. Leaving here,
                      they walked to 1 Canton Road and were not seen
                      out again by 12.30 a.m. when the watch was
                      terminated.

针对 CARPI 和 CONTINI，对广东路 1 号实施监视

1932年6月19日。未见任何重要人物进出该处所。

1932年6月20日。上午10时50分，有人看见 CARPI 和 CONTINI 离开该处所，前往位于广东路的罗伯特·道尔轮船公司大楼（Robert Dollar Line Building），CARPI 进入楼内，而 CONTINI 留在外面。十分钟后，他们前往中央商场（Central Arcade），从南京路与四川路入口处进入；两人均上楼，停留约五分钟。随后 CONTINI 返回广东路 1 号，而 CARPI 则乘电车前往大使剧院（Embassy Theatre）。下午1时30分探员用午餐时，他尚未离开剧院。下午2时35分，CONTINI 离开广东路 1 号，前往广东路 39 号——一处办公大楼——并在那里停留至下午3时。随后有人看见他返回广东路 1 号。下午3时10分，他步行至江西路 452 号——办公室——进入其中，仅停留数分钟。离开该处所后，他前往四川路 116 号的 F. Venturi & Co.，随后又前往金记路（Jinkee Road）35 号——一处容纳多间办公室的处所。约十分钟后，他返回其位于广东路 1 号的住所。此后直至下午6时30分监视结束，未再见到两人中的任何一人。

1932年6月21日。上午9时45分，有人看见 CARPI 和 CONTINI 离开广东路 1 号，前往汉口路 11 号的 Noel, Murray & Co. 拍卖行，在那里停留约十分钟。离开后，他们前往九江路 15 号的美国运通公司（American Express Co.）。CARPI 进入该处所，而 CONTINI 留在外面。几分钟后，CARPI 出来，与 CONTINI 一同前往九江路与江西路转角处，有人看见前者交给后者一些钱。
两人于上午10时10分左右分手。CONTINI 乘公共汽车前往静安寺路 939 号的高加索旅馆（Kavkaz Hotel）。上午11时，他返回中区，前往江西路的 L. Moore and Co. 拍卖行，在那里再次遇见 CARPI。
随后他们登上一辆向西行驶的公共汽车，车速过快，探员无法跟踪。下午3时，CARPI 返回广东路 1 号，并停留在该处所直至晚上9时20分，此时他在妻子陪同下，沿外滩前往外滩公园（Bund Gardens）；折返途中，他们在四川路的灰姑娘餐厅（Cinderella Restaurant）停下并进入用餐，直至晚上11时50分。离开此处后，他们步行回到广东路 1 号，直至凌晨12时30分监视结束时，未再见到他们外出。

page_data.en:
(2)

CONTINI returned to 1 Canton Road at
6.40 p.m. and remained there until 7.45 p.m.
when he took a ricksha to the Cinderella Res-
taurant, Szechuen Road, where he remained for
some five minutes. Leaving, he proceeded to
the Nanking Theatre where a violin recital
was being given by Mme. Chemet. He returned
to Canton Road at midnight when the watch was
terminated.

June 22, 1932. CARPI
At 3.55 p.m. CARPI made his way to 26 The
Bund, premises housing a block of offices,
where he remained about 20 minutes, returning
on foot to 1 Canton Road.
At 9 p.m. CARPI and his wife proceeded
to the Carlton Theatre by tramcar. After the
performance, they partook of refreshments in
the Foreign "Y", returning home by ricksha at
12.40 a.m. when the watch was terminated.

CONTINI
At 9.45 a.m. CONTINI made his way to the
Post Office at 71 Rue du Consulat and thence to
112 Szechuen Road - offices - returning to 1
Canton Road at 10.35 a.m.
At 11.20 a.m. CONTINI and CARPI proceeded
to 231 Szechuen Road ("China Theatres") where
they remained until 12.5 p.m. when they returned
to 1 Canton Road.
At 5.10 p.m. CONTINI walked to 116 Szechuen
Road and was seen talking to one AZZARETI, the
manager of Venturi & Co.
Leaving here at 6 p.m. he made his way to
the Palace Bar where he remained until 8 p.m.
when he returned to 1 Canton Road.
At 9 a.m. he made his way by bus to the
Nanking Theatre where he remained until the
performance had been completed. He then
returned to 1 Canton Road when the watch was
terminated.

June 24, 1932.
At 10.20 a.m. CARPI made his way by ricksha
to 36 Jinkee Road where he remained until
11.10 a.m. He then proceeded on foot to 116
Szechuen Road (F. Venturi & Co.) where he stayed
until 2.30 p.m. when he left and made his way
by ricksha to 452 Kiangse Road. He returned to
1 Canton Road at 3.15 p.m. and was not seen to
leave the premises again up till midnight when
the watch was terminated.

At 10.30 a.m. CONTINI made his way to
the Post Office at 71 Rue du Consulat, where
he purchased a quantity of postage stamps.
Leaving, he slowly made his way to the
Chocolate Shop on Nanking Road. He left here
at 11.40 a.m. and walked to F. Venturi & Co.,
116 Szechuen Road and was seen talking with
Azzareti for about 20 minutes, after which he
returned to Canton Road which he reached at
12.25 p.m.
page_data.zh:
(2)

CONTINI 于下午6时40分返回广东路 1 号，并停留至晚上7时45分，随后他乘坐人力车前往四川路的灰姑娘餐厅（Cinderella Restaurant），在那里停留约五分钟。离开后，他前往南京大戏院（Nanking Theatre），当时 Chemet 夫人正在那里举行小提琴独奏会。午夜时分他返回广东路，监视随即结束。

1932年6月22日。CARPI
下午3时55分，CARPI 前往外滩 26 号，这是一处容纳多间办公室的处所，他在那里停留约20分钟，随后步行返回广东路 1 号。
晚上9时，CARPI 与其妻子乘电车前往卡尔登大戏院（Carlton Theatre）。演出结束后，他们在青年会（Foreign "Y"）享用茶点，并于凌晨12时40分乘人力车回家，此时监视结束。

CONTINI
上午9时45分，CONTINI 前往领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）71 号的邮局，随后前往四川路 112 号——办公室——并于上午10时35分返回广东路 1 号。
上午11时20分，CONTINI 和 CARPI 前往四川路 231 号（“中国影戏公司” China Theatres），在那里停留至中午12时05分，随后返回广东路 1 号。
下午5时10分，CONTINI 步行至四川路 116 号，有人看见他与 Venturi & Co. 的经理 AZZARETI 交谈。
下午6时离开此处后，他前往宫殿酒吧（Palace Bar），并在那里停留至晚上8时，随后返回广东路 1 号。
[注：此处原文时间逻辑似有倒置或笔误，依原文翻译] 上午9时，他乘公共汽车前往南京大戏院，一直停留至演出结束。随后他返回广东路 1 号，此时监视结束。

1932年6月24日。
上午10时20分，CARPI 乘人力车前往金记路（Jinkee Road）36 号，并在那里停留至上午11时10分。随后他步行前往四川路 116 号（F. Venturi & Co.），在那里停留至下午2时30分，随后离开并乘人力车前往江西路 452 号。他于下午3时15分返回广东路 1 号，直至午夜监视结束，未再见到他离开该处所。

上午10时30分，CONTINI 前往领事馆路（Rue du Consulat）71 号的邮局，购买了一些邮票。
离开后，他缓慢前往南京路上的巧克力店。他于上午11时40分离开此处，步行前往四川路 116 号的 F. Venturi & Co.，有人看见他与 Azzareti 交谈约20分钟，之后他返回广东路，于中午12时25分到达。

He remained inside the premises until
3.30 p.m. when he again made his way to 116
Szechuen Road. Here the agent lost sight
of him and he was next seen to leave Canton
Road at 9.10 p.m. when he made his way to
Tkachenko's Cafe, Avenue Joffre. He remained
here until 11.30 p.m. when he returned to
Canton Road. The watch was then terminated.

FRANCESCO CONTINI, Italian
I Canton Rd.-He arrived in Shanghai about six years ago as a
chorus singer in the Italian Opera Company under the management
of Mr.Adolfo Carpi, Italian.
During the last three years, after the disbandment of the Opera
Company, he has had no fixed job.Nominally, he is a Secretary to
his former impresario, A.Carpi.
He is married to a Russian woman and speaks Russian.
He went to Italy few months ago and came back to Shanghai two
months ago.

ADOLFO CARPI, Italian
I Canton Rd.-Impresario.-During the last three years he has not
done any kind of work.He is never permanently in Shanghai, as he
travels a lot, going to North China, Harbin, Japan etc.etc.
Three years ago the French Police gave a confidential information
to the Italian Consulate General that Mr.A.Carpi was probably
acting as an agent for the Bolsheviks.A search was made at his
house without any result.
Mr.A.Carpi has resided many years in Russia and speaks excellent
Russian.

FRANCESCO CONTINI，意大利人
广东路 1 号——他约于六年前抵达上海，作为由意大利人 Adolfo Carpi 先生管理的意大利歌剧团的合唱歌手。
在过去三年中，自歌剧团解散后，他没有固定工作。名义上，他是其前经理人 A. Carpi 的秘书。
他娶了一位俄罗斯女子为妻，并能说俄语。
他于几个月前前往意大利，并于两个月前回到上海。

ADOLFO CARPI，意大利人
广东路 1 号——经理人。——在过去三年中，他未从事任何种类的工作。他从不长期定居上海，因为他经常旅行，前往华北、哈尔滨、日本等地。
三年前，法国警方曾向意大利总领事馆提供机密情报，称 A. Carpi 先生可能充当布尔什维克的代理人。对其住所进行了搜查，但未发现任何结果。
A. Carpi 先生曾在俄罗斯居住多年，并能说流利的俄语。

CONFIDENTIAL
November 26, 30.

Sir,

A. Carpi and M. A. Lourie-Stingoff

I have the honour to refer to your letter No. 3499,
dated November 11, 1930, and to state that there is nothing
in the records of the Municipal Police against A. Carpi or
any member of the cast in 1929 of Carpi's Opera Company.

However, enquiries show that Carpi has been sharing
an apartment at No. 1 Canton Road since April 1929 with one
M. A. Lourie-Stingoff. The latter is known to be an
enthusiastic Soviet worker, and it is more than likely that
he has used his influence with Carpi to find employment
under the latter for "Red" singers and dancers.

It is reported that Carpi is at present organizing
a Musical Revue Company with which he will tour Manila
and Java in the near future. The Musical Revue Company
will consist of sixteen members, but the names of these
are not yet available.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Officer-in-Charge
( Special Branch )

Shanghai.

Sir,
With reference to the attached letter of November
11, 1930 from the Consulate General for the Netherlands
concerning A. Carpi and the members of his Opera Company,
enquiries show that there is no evidence available regarding
the alleged relations between Carpi and Communist agents,
except the fact that M.A. Lourie-Ettingoff, a well known
Soviet Agent, has resided at Carpi's house, 1 Canton Road,
since April 1929.
A report is on record that Carpi and Lourie-Ettingoff
met about 12 or 13 years ago in Harbin where they were engaged
in some business the exact nature of which was not established.
Enquiries have failed to establish the existence
of any relations of a political character between Carpi and
Lourie-Ettingoff, but it is believed that some of the Soviet
agents may be introduced by the latter into Carpi's troupe
under the guise of singers, dancers etc.
It is reported that Carpi is at present organising
a Musical Revue Company which will consist of 16 members and
with which he intends to go to Manila and Java in the near
future. The list of members of that company is not yet
definitely known.
There is nothing in Municipal Police records to
the detriment of any of the members of Carpi's Opera Company
of 1929.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 12, 1928

ITALIAN GRAND OPERA
COMPANY

Mr. Adolfo Carpi, well-known
impresario, has organized a new
Italian Opera company for the 1929
season. The company has already
left Milan bound for Manila where
the season will commence early in
January and from Manila the opera
will play at Hongkong and then to
Shanghai, arriving here about the
beginning of February.

The company, we are told, has
acquired some very excellent singers
who have been loudly acclaimed both
by press and public in Europe etc.
Mr. Carpi has spared no pains and
expense in making the new company
one of the best to visit the Orient.
Scenery and costumes costing over
$50,000 have been provided for the
new organization.

After the conclusion of their
Shanghai season the company will
go to Tokyo to fulfil a three months'
engagement at the Imperial Theatre.
It is nearly two years since Shang-
hai was visited by an opera com-
pany and the return of Mr. Carpi
and his colleagues should be wel-
comed.
